thread:
ashley: Customer (AcmeCorp, acct_id=987654) reports promo code ACMEFW-50 is rejected as "invalid/expired" when they call the API to redeem. Dashboard (UI) shows 12 uses left. Ticket #12345. Request ID from customer: req_0a1b2c. Happened at 2025-09-14T15:02:21Z.

liz: Can you paste the exact API request + response you got from the customer? also which org/account?

ashley: Paste from customer support transcript: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/redeem \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"code":"ACMEFW-50","account_id":"987654"}'
```
Response body: `400 {"error":"promo_invalid_or_expired","detail":"code not found or expired","request_id":"req_0a1b2c"}`

ashley: Dashboard screenshot attached in ticket shows 12 remaining at 15:01:58Z; customer tried at 15:02:21Z. They said they clicked redeem from our hosted checkout and then retried via API when that failed.

rohit: I can take a look. Can you also paste the promo internal id or slug (from dashboard) and the event stream around that epoch? suspect concurrency/quota mismatch, not pure expiry.

ashley: Promo internal id `promo_333_acmefw`. From events near that time (pulled from support logs):
- 2025-09-14T15:01:59Z redeem success (user X)
- 2025-09-14T15:02:00Z redeem success (user Y)
- 2025-09-14T15:02:20Z customer redeem attempt (AcmeCorp) -> 400 invalid/expired
- 2025-09-14T15:02:22Z dashboard read shows remaining=0 for some users

liz: Hmm that's a tight window. dashboard uses cached_remaining_count (1m TTL) and the promo detail page can show stale numbers. Could be two parallel redeems that drained final uses. But customer says dashboard showed 12 before they tried; that suggests the cache was stale the other way (showing more than reality).

rohit: Looking at DB and audit logs: promo_333 had `max_uses = 12`. Two quick redeems at 15:01:59 and 15:02:00 were recorded, but we also have a small window where a background job that recomputes `cached_remaining` lags behind the real-time decrements. The UI path reads cached_remaining; the API redeem path does a check against `remaining_count` and then performs an atomic decrement. In this case the API rejects because remaining_count had hit 0 right before Acme tried. So the dashboard showed stale value (12) for ~20s due to cache not being invalidated on every write.

rohit: Root cause: we allowed eventual-consistency on the dashboard count and did not invalidate/update cache immediately on high-concurrency redeems. Race condition plus high parallel redeems exhausted the pool. Fix: update the redeem path to publish an immediate cache invalidation / update event and switch the write to use an atomic DB decrement (FOR UPDATE) to avoid slip-through. I'll open a small patch.

rohit: Created PR #4521 (eng-infra) with two changes: 1) atomic decrement in promo service to guarantee single-writer decrement; 2) immediate cache invalidation/publish on successful redeem. Will roll out to prod in patch window today.

mina: For customer impact: we can grant AcmeCorp an equivalent manual credit and mark the incident. I applied a 1-month credit of 50% billing credit to acct 987654 and updated ticket #12345. Billing adjustment id: adj_7890.

billing-bot: Manual credit applied -> adj_7890; note: credit posts within 2 hours.

ashley: Confirmed with customer that we applied the credit and explained the race condition. They accepted the credit and want to be notified when fix is live.

rohit: I'll push the patch to staging now, run a quick high-concurrency test, then ship to prod during the 17:00 UTC deploy window.

liz: Thanks team. I'll add notes to the promo docs advising that UI counts can be momentarily stale and update support playbook with the manual-credit workaround.

ashley: Closing loop with the customer and marking ticket resolved pending prod deploy. :white_check_mark:
